# Muhammad Huzaifa Shafique

> Graduate student in AI at Pittsburg State University (Master of Science in Technology, emphasis in AI, GPA 4.0, graduating December 2026), looking for AI and machine learning engineer roles. Builds retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), forecasting and threat-triage systems in Python, tests them against baselines, and states where they fall short.

- Site: https://muhammad-huzaifa-shafique.github.io/
- GitHub: https://github.com/Muhammad-Huzaifa-Shafique
- LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/muhammad-huzaifa-shafique

## Main projects

- [Casefile](https://muhammad-huzaifa-shafique.github.io/casefile.html): A local RAG assistant that answers penetration-testing questions from public documentation (HackTricks wiki and tool manual pages) and cites its sources. 22,720 chunks, three embedding setups (nomic-embed-text, nomic-embed-text with prefixes, all-minilm) in Chroma, Llama 3.1 8B served by Ollama, and a citation checker with 58 unit tests. Limits: seven test questions, no answer key, answer quality not measured end to end. Code: https://github.com/Muhammad-Huzaifa-Shafique/Penetration_Testing
- [CyberAI](https://muhammad-huzaifa-shafique.github.io/cyberai.html): Machine-learning threat triage with a human-review queue and an assistant that cites its evidence. Logistic regression, Isolation Forest anomaly detection, a drift monitor, TF-IDF retrieval (a MiniLM embedding index was built, but the chat does not use it in this version). Limits: no saved evaluation, and the saved training data (25 malicious file hashes, 425 unlabeled text records) cannot support a meaningful test, so no accuracy is claimed; the full pipeline source is not published yet. Code: https://github.com/Muhammad-Huzaifa-Shafique/CyberAI
- [Sales forecasting with a neural network](https://muhammad-huzaifa-shafique.github.io/forecasting.html): A scikit-learn MLPRegressor that forecasts monthly sales for ten items, tested against four baselines on 12 unseen months with MAE, RMSE, WAPE and bias. WAPE 78.7% against 89.6% for the best baseline (about 12% lower). Five model versions, one rejected. Limits: bias of -37% over the test year, one hold-out period, ten items. Code: https://github.com/Muhammad-Huzaifa-Shafique/Sales-Forecasting-Neural-Network
- [Gapminder dashboard](https://muhammad-huzaifa-shafique.github.io/dashboard.html): An animated Quarto, R and Plotly report on life expectancy and income in 142 countries, 1952 to 2007, with population-weighted continent averages and a log income scale. Code: https://github.com/Muhammad-Huzaifa-Shafique/Dashboard

## Deep learning coursework

- [Neural networks from a NumPy forward pass to Keras CNNs](https://muhammad-huzaifa-shafique.github.io/deep-learning.html): An interactive walkthrough of four graduate neural-network assignments. (1) A 3-4-4-1 network's forward pass in NumPy. (2) Backpropagation written by hand with a 500-epoch gradient-descent loop on 100 synthetic samples: training loss falls from 796.2 to 23.5, after a long flat start at the variance of the targets and a one-epoch spike at epoch 121. (3) Ten one-change Keras experiments on California housing prices, each kept only if validation MAPE improved: test MAPE 21.33% to 18.91%. (4) Ten convolutional-network variations on CIFAR-10: test accuracy 71.65% to 74.54%. Limits: course exercises on standard datasets; each Keras result is a single training run; assignment 4 has no validation set, so its best score is probably a little optimistic; the Keras numbers are copied from the submitted reports. Code: https://github.com/Muhammad-Huzaifa-Shafique/Neural-Networks-Coursework

## Data engineering

- [Oklahoma legislature vote extractor](https://muhammad-huzaifa-shafique.github.io/data-engineering.html): Python (asyncio, aiohttp, regular expressions, pandas) tool that collects House and Senate votes into three CSV files. Team project in a graduate course; my part was the House votes. Checks on the House output (30,475 votes, 1999 to 2025): seat counts add up to the size of the House, but member rows cover only 76% of counted seats, and the cause is not yet traced. Code: https://github.com/Muhammad-Huzaifa-Shafique/Oklahoma-Legislature-Vote-Extractor
- [Fixed-width data extractor](https://muhammad-huzaifa-shafique.github.io/data-engineering.html#fixed): Turns fixed-width text reports into clean Excel tables. Code: https://github.com/Muhammad-Huzaifa-Shafique/Fixed-Width-Data-Extractor

## How I work with AI

- [Prompts, checks and disclosure](https://muhammad-huzaifa-shafique.github.io/method.html): Four real prompts from my projects, line by line, with what each line is for and what checks it, plus how I use AI assistants when I write code and reports. I have not compared prompt wordings against a scored test set.

## Skills

- Machine learning and LLMs: scikit-learn (neural networks, logistic regression, Isolation Forest), time-series feature engineering, model evaluation (MAE, RMSE, WAPE, MAPE, bias, baselines, hold-out tests), anomaly detection, drift monitoring, human-in-the-loop review, retrieval-augmented generation, embeddings and vector search (Chroma, MiniLM, nomic-embed-text), TF-IDF retrieval, prompt engineering, citation checking, local LLMs (Ollama, Llama 3.1).
- Deep learning (coursework): neural networks, forward propagation and backpropagation written in NumPy, gradient descent, regression and convolutional neural networks (CNN) in Keras and TensorFlow, early stopping, dropout, batch normalization, learning-rate schedules, data augmentation, hyperparameter experiments, CIFAR-10 image classification.
- Python and data: Python, pandas, NumPy, SQL, SQLite, R, Quarto, Plotly, REST APIs, Flask, asyncio, unit testing, Git.
- Security: penetration testing, vulnerability assessment, threat intelligence, Kali Linux, Nmap, Metasploit.
